purpose: Deterministic byte-encoding and SHA-512 derivation conformance vector. Synthetic certificate/key byte strings are used only to test derivation; they are not valid credentials and MUST NOT be used for authentication.
encoding: For every ordered field: uint32_be(length(field_bytes)) || field_bytes. SHA-512 over the concatenation. Candidate IPv6 address is the first 16 digest bytes in network byte order.

candidates.reason: Candidate is outside the required 2000::/3 policy prefix.
The address is inside 2000::/3; implementation must still check every pinned policy exclusion before accepting it.

negative_requirements: Changing any one input field must change the encoded input and normally the digest; do not treat digest equality as an authorization decision.
Changing field order must fail the vector.
Removing a uint32 length prefix or using little-endian/native-endian lengths must fail the vector.
Encoding time_bucket as text or as a non-8-byte integer must fail the vector.
Using the raw text form of an IPv6 address instead of its 16 packed bytes must fail the vector.
Using a nonce other than 32 bytes must be rejected before derivation.
Candidate policy rejection must redraw a fresh nonce; it must not mask or rewrite digest bits.

These vectors validate derivation encoding only. They do not validate certificate parsing, signature verification, RDR authenticity, M1 schema, time freshness, nonce replay prevention, or the complete address exclusion table.
